title: Richards Fixed-Horizon Nested Refinement Certificate Characterization

scientific_trigger.finding: Changing the outer attempted endpoint during retry does not preserve a conservative relation between raw one-versus-two-step head defect and fine-reference error across the held-out hydraulic envelope.

source_bound_prior_evidence.key_observation: At fixed physical t1, successive Richards trajectories refine toward one another. The dry state is pre-asymptotically under-conservative for early raw defects but enters a conservative regime after further fixed-horizon refinement.

candidate_semantics.name: FIXED_HORIZON_NESTED_REFINEMENT_BAND
candidate_semantics.attempt_origin: single physical base state at attempt t0
candidate_semantics.attempt_endpoint: single unchanged physical t1 for every internal refinement trajectory
candidate_semantics.primary_dimensional_observable: d_k = max_i abs(h_N_i - h_2N_i) at common final t1
candidate_semantics.candidate_band_question: Does a bounded sequence of successive fixed-horizon endpoint defects enter and remain in a contracting, non-pathological regime across the prescribed-head hydraulic envelope?

required_outputs_per_case: all nested trajectories converged or explicit solver-failure level
first level with two consecutive decreases
first level with three consecutive decreases
comparison against a finer same-horizon reference for characterization only

gate_B_if_A_supports_candidate.type: certificate-shape experiment through qualified F-KT09 seam
